section_prompt:
Bandera nazionala herrialde bat ordezkatzen duen bandera da. Banderaren koloreek eta diseinuek herrialdeen historia eta gaur egungo egoera deskribatzen dituzte. Herrialde subiranoaren ikurra denez, bandera nazionalak herrialdea eta bertako herritarrak atzerrian ordezkatzen ditu. Historia, kultura, etnia edo erlijioa partekatzen dituzten herrialde askok lotura hori sinbolizatzen duten antzeko koloreak eta diseinuak dituzte. Banderek jatorria gudu-zelaietan dute, ikur militarrak bezala erabiltzen baitziren; gaur egun, ordea, testuinguru ez-militarretan ere ageri dira, hala nola eraikin publikoetan zein ospakizunetan. Gertaera nazional tragiko bat jazotzean edo omendu nahi den norbait hiltzen denean, bandera nazionala haga erdian jartzen da dolu-seinale moduan. 
Nazio batzuetan, bandera argiztatuta egon ezean, gauez jaistera derrigortuta daude legez. Euria edo haizeak kaltetu ditzakeenean ere jaitsi behar izaten dute. Bandera nazional guztiak angeluzuzenak dira, Nepaleko triangeluarra izan ezik. Suitzakoak zein Vatikano Hirikoak lauki perfektuaren forma dute. Zabalera eta altueraren neurriak batetik bestera aldatzen badira ere, kasu orotan zabalera altuera baino luzeagoa da.
section_prompt_translated: The national flag is the flag that represents a country. The colours and design of the flag describe the history and current situation of countries. As it is the sign of the sovereign country, the national flag represents the country and its citizens abroad. Many countries that share their history, culture, ethnic and religion have similar colours and designs. Flags have their origin in battlefields, as they were used as military signs; nowadays, however, they are also present in non-military contexts, e.g., in public buildings or celebrations. When a national tragedy occurs or someone dies, the national flag flies at half-mast as a sign of mourning. In some nations, if the flag is not illuminated, it is compulsory to bring it down at night. If the rain or wind may damage them, they should also be pulled down.  All national flags are right-angled, except for the one from Nepal, which is triangular. The ones from Switzerland and Vatican have a perfect square shape. Although it may vary from one flag to another, they are generally wider than long.

The International Union for the Conservation of Nature is an international organization dedicated to the conservation of nature and the sustainable use of natural resources. Participates in data collection and analysis, research, field projects, promotion, and education.
Its mission is "not only to influence, promote and support societies around the world in the conservation of nature, but to ensure that all use of natural resources is equitable and ecologically sustainable". In recent decades, the organization has expanded its vision beyond the ecology of conservation and incorporates issues related to sustainable development into its projects. Unlike many other international environmental organizations, it does not aim to mobilize the population for the conservation of nature. Instead, the organization tries to influence the actions of governments, businesses and other shareholders through information, advice, and the construction of partnerships. The organization is best known for the collection and publication of the "Red List of Threatened Species", which assesses the conservation status of species worldwide. Today, the organization is made up of a thousand workers from more than fifty countries working full-time.

section_prompt: Shaka Hawaiiko kultura eta surf kirolarekin loturiko keinua da. Jatorria uharte hauetan duela badirudi ere, hogeigarren mendearen erdialdetik aurrera mundu osoko surflarien artean hedatu zen. Bere jatorriaren inguruko tradizio popularrenak dioenez, azukre lantegi batean trena zaintzen ziharduen gizon bati erdiko hiru hatzak falta zitzaizkion, eta beste biak altxatzen zituen dena libre zegoela adierazteko. Gerora shaka keinua bilakatu zen.  Esku bateko hatz lodia eta txikia luzatu eta gainontzekoak itxita mantenduz egiten da. Keinua egin bitartean eskua zeharka astinduz nabarmenago egiten da. Egun esanahi anitz ditu keinu honek eta, herrialdearen edo komunitatearen arabera, izena eta esanahia ere alda daitezke: Txinan, adibidez, sei zenbakia irudikatzen du; Errusian, berriz, garagardo bat hartzeko gonbita, eta Karibeko uharte batzuetan sexu harremana. Hawaiiko biztanleek keinua «Aloha Espiritua» deritzotena adierazteko darabilte. Zehatzago esanda, bertan bizi diren kultura etniko anitzen artean adiskidetasuna, elkartasuna eta errukiaren esanahia du kontzeptuak. Shaka keinua belaunaldiz belaunaldi transmititu da. Zeinuak oraindik ere Hawaiiko maitaleak elkartzen ditu tradizio bakarrarekin.
section_prompt_translated: The Shaka sign is associated with Hawaiian culture and surf. Even if its origin may be in these islands, it has spread among surfers worldwide after the second half of the 20th century. According to the most popular traditions about its origin, a worker guarding the train at a sugar factory was missing three fingers and used to lift the other two to indicate when the train rail was free. It later became the Shaka sign. It consists of lifting the thumb and the smallest finger and keeping the others curled. When doing the sign, the hand may be shaken back and forth for emphasis. Nowadays, this sign has various meanings and, depending on the country or community, the name and meaning can also change: in China, for example, it represents number 6; in Russia, however, it is an invitation to have a beer and, in some Caribbean islands, to sexual intercourse.  Hawaiian citizens use it to express what they call the “Aloha Spirit”. More specifically, among the local variety of ethnic cultures, this concept means friendship, solidarity, and mercy. The Shaka sign has been transmitted from generation to generation. This sign still brings together Hawaiian lovers with a unique tradition.

section_prompt_translated: Thylacinus cynocephalus, in English Tasmanian tiger (for its striped back), Tasmanian wolf or marsupial wolf (canid-like face and characteristics),  could be considered as the biggest carnivorous marsupial of the Modern Age. It is believed that it became extinct in Australia in the 20th century, when the British entered the continent and settled. The Tasmanian tiger was fawn-coloured, between yellow-brown and grey, and had dark stripes from the back to the tail. Although its big head gave it a dog or wolf-like  appearence, it had a straight tail and fairly short legs. Its body hair was dense, short and soft. It had short ears (around 80mm long), round and covered in short hair. It is still unknown why it disappeared from the Australian continent. Maybe it disappeared due to the competition with the dingos or the pressure caused by human hunting.

Hirugarrena, markorik gabeko pieza bakarreko kristala zen, normalean inongo euskalurik gabea. Orokorrean goi-mailako gizon aberatsek erabiltzen zuten, kapela luzeak eta frakak lagunduta. Gaur egun, optometrian egondako aurrerapenei esker batez ere, monokuloak ez dira ohikoak.
section_prompt_translated: The monocle is a single lens used to correct the vision in one eye. It is worn only on that eye. There are three types of monocles. The first one was a metal ring with a lens that got adjusted to the eye-orbit. The second monocle had an extension in the frame, known as the gallery. This prevented eyelashes from touching the lens. The third was a frameless glass, normally with no cord. An antiquarian named Philipp von Stosch wore the monocle in Rome in the 1720s to better observe antiques. In the 1790s it became fashionable among high-class dandies. It was not until the 19th that the monocle became known among men. In general, high-class rich men used it, together with long hats and trousers. Nowadays, thanks mainly to the advances in optometry, monocles are uncommon.

section_prompt: O sinal de shaka, conhecido no Brasil como hang loose", é um gesto usado tipicamente por surfistas e praieiros para saudações em geral. O sinal é feito com uma das mãos com o polegar e o dedo mindinho estendidos, enquanto os demais dedos ficam fechados, formando um gesto parecido com a letra Y. O hang loose já foi usado como símbolo de campanha política, sinal de lutadores de luta livre e em comemorações por jogadores de futebol. A origem exata do gesto é desconhecida, conhecendo-se apenas algumas teorias. A tradição havaiana predominante atribui o gesto a um homem que perdeu os três dedos do meio de sua mão quando trabalhava colhendo açúcar. Por isso o homem passou a vigiar os carros de açúcar, e quando eles estavam completamente esvaziados ele fazia o gesto, como quisesse dizer, “tudo bem”. Com o passar dos anos, ficou conhecido como o shaka. Uma segunda teoria vincula o sinal do “hang loose” com um jogo de canecas, onde a posição das mãos, formava o shaka. Uma terceira teoria, consiste no termo “shark eye” (olho de tubarão). Ao fazer o gesto, representava a cabeça do tubarão martelo, muito respeitado na cultura havaiana."
section_prompt_translated: The sign of shaka, known in Brazil as "hang loose", is a gesture used typically by surfers and beach goers as general salutation. The sign is made on one hand with the thumb and pinkie extended, while the other fingers are closed, forming a gesture resembling a Y. The hang loose has been used as a symbol in political campaigns, by martial arts fighters, and by celebrated football players. The exact origin of the gesture is unknown, only a few speculative theories exist. A predominant hawaiian tradition atributed the gesture to men who had lost their three middle fingers from harvesting sugar. The men who checked sugar carts would make this gesture to indicate "all good" when the carts where completely empty. After the years it became known as the shaka. A second theory connects the "hang loose" sign with a set of mugs, where hand positions formed the shaka. A third theory, consists of the term "shark eye". Making the gesture represents the head of a hammerhead shark, a highly respected figure in Hawaiian culture.

The male has a pouch that acted as a protective coat, protecting the external organs of the animal while he ran through the dense forest. section_prompt: O monóculo é um tipo de lente corretiva utilizados para corrigir a visão em apenas um olho. É constituída por uma lente circular, geralmente com um fio ao redor da circunferência do anel que pode ser associado a uma corda. A outra extremidade da corda é então ligada ao vestuário em uso para evitar a perda do monóculo. A origem da palavra vem do grego: “mónos”, único e do Latim: “oculu”, olho. Não se sabe ao certo a real data em que o monóculo foi criado, pois é uma invenção bem antiga e pouco utilizada devido ao fato de que é pequeno o número de pessoas com miopia em um globo ocular, mas estima-se que foi entre o século dezoito e dezenove. Um monge, que viveu no século dezoito, na obra mais científica elaborada na época, o Opus majus, referente às leis da refração e reflexão da luz, descreve o uso de lentes para corrigir os defeitos de visão. Essas lentes foram usadas durante vários séculos, inicialmente pelos monges copistas ou tradutores.
section_prompt_translated: A monocle is a type of corrective lens used to correct vision in only one eye. It consists of a circular lens, generally with a frame around the circumference of the ring that can be connected to a chain. The other end of the chain is then attached to the clothing in order to prevent the loss of the monocle. The origin of the word comes from the Greek: “mónos”, unique and from the Latin: “oculu”, eye. It is not known for certain the actual date when the monocle was created, as it is a very old invention and little used due to the fact that the number of people with myopia in one eye is small, but it is estimated that it was between the eighteenth and nineteenth century. A monk, who lived in the eighteenth century, describes the use of lenses to correct vision defects, referring to the laws of refraction and reflection of light in the most scientific work created at the time, the Opus majus. These lenses were used for several centuries, initially by scribes or translator monks.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: Apicultura é a ciência, ou arte, da criação de abelhas com ferrão e trata-se de um ramo da zootecnia. Não se sabe ao certo quando, mas eventualmente os humanos começaram a tentar domesticar abelhas silvestres em colmeias artificiais feitas de troncos ocos, caixas de madeira, vasos de cerâmica e cestos de palha ou “saches”. Vestígios de cera de abelha são encontrados em fragmentos de potes no Oriente Médio, começando por volta de sete milênios antes de Cristo. A criação racional de abelhas para o lazer, ou fins comerciais, pode ter como objetivo, por exemplo, a produção de mel, própolis, geleia real, pólen, cera de abelha e veneno, ou mesmo fazer parte de um projeto de paisagismo. No Brasil, esse projeto de paisagismo não é possível porque as abelhas africanizadas são mais defensivas e requer uma distância mínima de trezentos metros de qualquer aglomeração de pessoas e animais. Além disso, as abelhas são importantes polinizadoras. A maioria dos apicultores usam alguma roupa de proteção. Apicultores novatos geralmente usam luvas e um roupa fechada, chapéu e um véu com capuz, enquanto apicultores experientes, por vezes, optam por não usar luvas porque inibem manipulações delicadas.
section_prompt_translated: Beekeeping is the science, or art, of raising stinging bees and is a branch of animal husbandry. It is not known exactly when, but eventually humans began trying to domesticate wild bees in artificial hives made of hollow logs, wooden boxes, ceramic vases and straw baskets or “saches”. Traces of beeswax are found in pot fragments in the Middle East, beginning around seventh millennia BC. The rational breeding of bees for leisure, or commercial purposes, can aim, for example, at the production of honey, propolis, royal jelly, pollen, beeswax and poison, or even be part of a landscaping project. In Brazil, the landscaping projects are not possible because Africanized bees are more defensive and requires a minimum distance of three hundred meters from any gathering of people and animals. Furthermore, bees are important pollinators. Most beekeepers wear some protective clothing. Novice beekeepers generally wear gloves and a closed coat, a hat and a hooded veil, while experienced beekeepers sometimes choose not to wear gloves because they inhibit delicate manipulations.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: 沙卡手势，源自于夏威夷，做法就是把手的大拇指和小指伸直，其余的手指收起，看起来就像是数字六的手势，也可以加上左右摇动来强调，主要有「打招呼、祝好运、再见、放轻松」的意思。在一九六零年代时，沙卡手势开始流行于冲浪客之间，用来表达问候、表达感谢、认同、或赞美，后来渐渐地遍及全世界。关于沙卡手势的确切由来还存在争议，不过大多数人认为它起源于冲浪运动，和沙滩有关。也有一派说法，认为沙卡手势是来自西班牙移民，他们会把中指收起并将大拇指放在嘴唇上，做为友好的表现，代表要邀请夏威夷当地居民喝酒的意思。无论这个传达友好意图的手势是怎么来的，夏威夷人透过沙卡手势来传达「阿罗哈精神」，也就是强调友谊、理解、同情心、以及跨族群团结等概念的文化。
section_prompt_translated: Shaka signs, originated from Hawaii, it is done by straightening the thumb and little finger and bending the rest of the fingers inwards. Shaka looks like the “number six” gesture, it can also be emphasized by shaking your hand from left to right, but it’s mainly used to “greet people, wish others luck, say goodbyes, and relax”. In the 1960s, Shaka signs have begun to popularize among surfers; it is used to express greetings, gratitude, agreement; after that, the Shaka sign spread all over the world. The origin of Shaka signs remains controversial, but most people consider the source of Shaka sign from surfing exercise and associated with the beach. Others say Shaka signs came from Hispanic immigrants. Hispanic immigrants would often bend their middle finger inwards and place their thumbs on their lips as a sign of goodwill; it represents an invitation from the local Hawaiians to drink beverages. Regardless of the origins of this gesture, Hawaiians convey the spirit of Aloha through this hand gesture; it is also used to emphasize friendship, appreciation, compassion, and the unity of different cultures.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: 袋狼是近代体型最大的肉食有袋性动物，因其身上斑纹似虎，又名塔斯马尼亚虎，也因其外观和特征，被称为塔斯马尼亚狼。这种动物曾广泛分布于新几内亚热带雨林、澳大利亚草原、塔斯马尼亚岛等地，后来因人类将其视为敌人、并在政府的奖赏制度下被大量屠杀，也可能因传染病、和野狗竞争等因素，现已全部灭绝。袋狼和其他有袋动物一样，母体有育儿袋，不成熟的幼兽出生之后，在育儿袋中成长；公袋狼也有一个小袋，在牠们跑过树丛时可用来保护外生殖器官。袋狼为肉食性动物，据说牠的嘴巴张开幅度很大、有利撕咬，肚子上的肌肉和骨架也能有效地胀大，可吃下大量的食物。最后一只人工饲养的袋狼于1936年因动物园管理员的疏忽，在高温曝晒下死亡，其后数十年，人们一直搜寻袋狼的踪迹，但都未曾有可靠证据显示袋狼仍然存在，因此目前科学界普遍认为袋狼已经灭绝。
section_prompt_translated: Thylacines are the largest modern-day Marsupial carnivore; it has the stripes of a tiger, so it is also called Tasmania tiger. In addition, due to its appearance and features, it is known as Tasmania wolf. This kind of animal is scattered around the rainforest in New Guinea, savanna in Australia, and Tasmania. In the later years, humankind views Thylacine as hostile, and Thylacines are mass slaughtered under the bounty of government. Still, it might be due to infectious diseases or competitions with other wild dogs causing Thylacine to be extinct. Female Thylacine shares similarities with other Marsupial species by having a brood pouch to breed their offsprings. On the other hand, male Thylacine has thick furs covering their pouch to protect their sexual organs. Thylacines are carnivores; it is said that they could open their mouth very wide for biting. The muscle on their abdominal and bone structure helps them consume larger prays. Early scientific evidence suggests Thylacines are a nocturnal animal with sharp olfactory senses; this allows them to track kangaroo, wombat, bird, and other prey such as opossum. The last human-bred Thylacine died of high temperature in 1936 due to zookeepers’ oversight. Since then, after a few decades, people have been searching for traces of wild Thylacines, but there are no reliable evidences suggesting the existence of Thylacines; therefore, it is scientifically common to recognize the Thylacines as extincted.

section_prompt: 柳橙汁是从柳橙的果肉中榨出的果汁。商业贩卖的柳橙汁为了延长保存期限，会去除果汁内的氧气以杀菌，但此举将大大降低果汁的味道，因此通常会再添加由柳橙萃取出的人工香料到其中。除了这些加工步骤，有些果汁在制造的过程中，会先进行脱水、之后再加水到果汁中，或先将果汁浓缩、之后再加水到浓缩汁中。虽然柳橙汁含有大量的维生素C，但亦含有和其他非酒精饮料相当、很高浓度的糖分，故其健康价值还有待商榷。因此，尽管直接食用柳橙消化得相对较慢、每日可摄取的量也有限，但一些政府机关所提出的营养建议，已调整成鼓励民众直接食用柳橙、而非饮用柳橙汁。
section_prompt_translated: Orange juice is juice squeezed from orange meat. In order to extend the expiry date of commercially sold orange juice, the oxygen inside the juice will be extracted and sterilized, but this process will massively reduce the taste of the juice; therefore, it is common to add artificial flavor extracted from orange to the juice itself. Besides this processing, during the processing, some of the juice is dehydrated, then water will be added to the juice or condense the juice, then add water to the concentrated juice. Even though orange juice contains large amounts of vitamin C, but it also contains the equivalent of other sugar compared to other non-alcohol beverages; thus, the nutritional value remains in discussion. Therefore, direct consumption of oranges is relatively slow, and the amount of daily intake is limited, some government agencies have proposed nutritional recommendations that encourage people to eat an orange instead of orange juice.

The historical origin of a national flag is a military flag used in ancient warfare and it’s used as a symbol on the battlefield. instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: 沙卡手勢，源自於夏威夷，做法就是把手的大拇指和小指伸直，其餘的手指收起，看起來就像是數字六的手勢，也可以加上左右搖動來強調，主要有「打招呼、祝好運、再見、放輕鬆」的意思。在一九六零年代時，沙卡手勢開始流行於衝浪客之間，用來表達問候、表達感謝、認同、或讚美，後來漸漸地遍及全世界。關於沙卡手勢的確切由來還存在爭議，不過大多數人認為它起源於衝浪運動，和沙灘有關。也有一派說法，認為沙卡手勢是來自西班牙移民，他們會把中指收起並將大拇指放在嘴唇上，做為友好的表現，代表要邀請夏威夷當地居民喝酒的意思。無論這個傳達友好意圖的手勢是怎麼來的，夏威夷人透過沙卡手勢來傳達「阿羅哈精神」，也就是強調友誼、理解、同情心、以及跨族群團結等概念的文化。
section_prompt_translated: Shaka signs, originated from Hawaii, it is done by straightening the thumb and little finger and bending the rest of the fingers inwards. Shaka looks like the “number six” gesture, it can also be emphasized by shaking your hand from left to right, but it’s mainly used to “greet people, wish others luck, say goodbyes, and relax”. In the 1960s, Shaka signs have begun to popularize among surfers; it is used to express greetings, gratitude, agreement; after that, the Shaka sign spread all over the world. The origin of Shaka signs remains controversial, but most people consider the source of Shaka sign from surfing exercise and associated with the beach. Others say Shaka signs came from Hispanic immigrants. Hispanic immigrants would often bend their middle finger inwards and place their thumbs on their lips as a sign of goodwill; it represents an invitation from the local Hawaiians to drink beverages. Regardless of the origins of this gesture, Hawaiians convey the spirit of Aloha through this hand gesture; it is also used to emphasize friendship, appreciation, compassion, and the unity of different cultures.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: 自一九七四年起，聯合國將每年的六月五日定為世界環境日，以作為鼓勵全球居民提高環保意識和採取環保行動的主要力量，並利用此一重要的社會運動，提升人們對海洋污染、人口過剩、全球暖化等新興環境問題的認識。如今，全球有一百多個國家每年都參與世界環境日，讓這個活動成為向公眾推廣理念的國際化平台。在每一年的世界環境日，全世界的各大公司、非政府組織、各類團體、政府和社會名流都會根據該年選定的新主題，積極倡導環境議題。以二零一八年為例，該年世界環境日的主題是「塑戰速決」，目的是希望能夠將減塑行動落實在每個人的日常生活之中，拋棄圖一時方便的習慣，儘量減少使用一次性塑膠製品，共同來對抗塑膠製品對環境造成的嚴重後果和汙染。為響應此運動，印度政府已承諾到二零二二年時，一次性塑膠製品將在印度消失。
section_prompt_translated: From 1974, the United Nations has named June 5th World Environment Day, to encourage global residents to raise environmental awareness and take environmental actions. They are using this significant social movement to raise awareness of emerging environmental issues such as marine pollution, overpopulation, and global warming. Today, more than 100 countries are participating World Environment Day annually, making this event an international platform for promoting the concept to the public. Every year’s World Environment Day, every global company, a non-profit organization, all kinds of organization, government, and celebrities will choose the theme according to that year to advocate environmental issues. Take 2018 as an example; the topic of World Environment Day of that year is "Successful Warfare". The aim is to reduce the usage of plastic in daily life, to abandon the convenient habits and minimize the usage of disposable plastic products and fight the serious environmental consequences and pollution of plastic products. In response to this campaign, the Indian government has promised that by 2022, disposable plastic products will disappear in India.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: 單片眼鏡包括一個圓形透鏡，鏡片邊緣通常有一個可以連接到細繩或鍊子上的環框，而繩子的另一端則可以繫在配戴者的衣服上，避免鏡片遺失。單片眼鏡的功能，是用來矯正或增強視力，但在十九世紀晚期，單片眼鏡也被當作高社經背景的象徵，常可見到此時期富裕的上流階級男性和軍官配戴單片眼鏡。事實上，十九世紀晚期資本家典型的裝扮，便是配戴單片眼鏡，再搭配長大衣和禮帽。雖然單片眼鏡在十九世紀晚期蔚為風潮，但因為驗光技術的進步，現在人們已可以更精準地測量視力，以不同度數的眼鏡和隱形眼鏡來矯正兩隻眼睛不同程度的屈光錯誤，現在已很少有人配戴單片眼鏡。
section_prompt_translated: Monocle consists of an oval piece of glass; the edge of the lens usually has a frame that can be attached to a string or chain, while the other end of the rope can be attached to a person's clothing to avoid losing it. Still, in the 19th century, the monocle is viewed as a symbol of high social status; it is also commonly seen on upper social class and military background males during this period. The typical dress of the capitalists in the late 19th century was wearing monocles and matching long coats and top hats. Although monocles became more popular in the late 19th century, due to advancements in optometry, nowadays, people can measure vision more precisely and use a different kind of glasses and contact lenses to correct different degrees of refractive errors in both eyes. Nowadays, few people wear monocles.

section_prompt_translated: Orange juice is juice squeezed from orange meat. In order to extend the expiry date of commercially sold orange juice, the oxygen inside the juice will be extracted and sterilized, but this process will massively reduce the taste of the juice; therefore, it is common to add artificial flavor extracted from orange to the juice itself. section_prompt: Et nationalflag er et flag, som borgerne i et land har ret til at flage med på landjorden. Det repræsenterer og symboliserer et land. Danmarks flag kaldes for Dannebrog, hvad der betyder danernes fane eller rødfarvet fane. Dannebrog er rødt med et hvidt kors, der når ud til siderne af flaget. Korsflag kendes fra flere lande, men findes altovervejende i Nordeuropa, først og fremmest de andre nordiske lande: Finland, Sverige, Norge og Island samt de autonome områder Åland og Færøerne. Flaget menes normalt at stamme fra den danske korstogsperiode i ellevehundrede- til tolvhundredetallet. En udbredt skik er, at flaget først må hejses ved solopgang, dog aldrig tidligere end klokken otte om morgenen, og flaget tages ned senest ved solnedgang. Et flag kan godt forblive oppe, såfremt det er belyst med projektør eller lignende. Det er en udbredt skik, at Dannebrog aldrig må røre jorden, da flaget som udgangspunkt altid må behandles med værdighed.
section_prompt_translated: A national flag is a flag which the citizens of a country have the right to fly on land. It represents and symbolises a country. Denmark’s flag is called ‘Dannebrog’, which means the flag of the Danes or red coloured flag. Dannebrog is red with a white cross that reach the sides of the flag. Cross flags are known from several countries but are predominantly found in the other Nordic countries: Finland, Sweden, Norway and Iceland as well as the autonomous areas of Åland and the Faroe Islands. The flag is usually considered to derive from the Danish crusading period in the twelfth to the thirteenth centuries. No Danish legislation exists that directly regulates how citizens are allowed to fly Dannebrog, but a number of rules in single areas and custom cover a part of the use. A widespread custom is that the flag must not be raised before sunrise, but never earlier than 8 in the morning and the flag has to be lowered at sunset at the latest. A flag may be flown if it is bright or if the flag is lit by floodlights or similar. It is a widespread custom that Dannebrog may never touch the ground since the flag is always to be treated with dignity.

section_prompt: Thylacinus cynocephalus, eller den tasmanske pungulv var et stort rovdyr, der levede i Australien. På engelsk kaldes dyret den tasmanske tiger, men pungulven var hverken kat eller hund; som mange australske dyr hørte den til pungdyrene som kænguruen og vombatten. I tidsperioden sen pleistocæn til tidlig holocæn var pungulve almindelige i Australien, men da befolkningen fra nordliggende øer introducerede dingoen i Australien for omkring fem tusind år siden, blev pungulven udsat for hård konkurrence, og populationen af pungulve faldt. Det er usikkert, hvornår den sidste pungulv døde i Australien, men det kan have været så sent som for ca. tusind år siden. På Tasmanien, hvor dingoen ikke var blevet indført, overlevede pungulven helt op til vores tid. I de sidste år var også samleres indhug i bestanden en væsentlig årsag til den endelige udryddelse. I udseende mindede pungulven om en korthåret hund med en stiv hale, der mest lignede en kængurus hale. På bagparten havde pungulven striber. De kraftige kæber kunne åbnes i en næsten halvfems graders vinkel, og pungen vendte bagud.
section_prompt_translated: Thylacinus cynocephalus, or the Tasmanian Wolf was a large predator that lived in Australia. In English the animal is called the Tasmanian Tiger but the Thylacine was neither cat nor canid; like many Australian animals, it belonged to the marsupials like kangaroos or wombats. In the period of late Pleistocene to early Holocene, Thylacines were common in Australia but when the inhabitants from northern islands introduced Dingos to Australia around five thousand years ago, Thylacines were exposed to tough competition and the population of Thylacines plummeted. It is uncertain when the last Thylacine died in Australia, but it may have been as late as approx. one thousand years ago. In Tasmania, where Dingos were not introduced, the Thylacine survived until our time. In the last years, collectors making a dent in the population were also a major contributing factor to its final extinction. In appearance, the Thylacine resembled a shorthaired dog with a stiff tail that most of all looked like a kangaroo tail. On the rear end, the Thylacine had stripes. The powerful jaws could open to almost a 90 degrees angle and the pouch faced backwards.

section_prompt_translated: A monocle is a single spectacle lens which is worn over one eye. The monocle is a corrective lens that is used to improve the sight in one eye. Lenses of rock crystal had then long been used as vision aids.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: Biavl er menneskets opretholdelse af honningbifamilier, almindeligvis i bistader. En biavler holder bier med det formål at indsamle honning og bivoks for at bestøve afgrøder eller for at producere bier og bifamilier med salg for øje til andre biavlere. Lokaliteten, hvor bier holdes, kaldes for en bigård. Biavlens og biavleres skytshelgen er Skt. Ambrosius. Domesticering af bier er afbildet i egyptisk kunst for over fire tusind år siden. I adskillige årtusinder var menneskets forståelse af biernes biologi og økologi meget begrænset, og denne forståelse var præget af overtro og folklore. Oldtidens mennesker troede, at bidronningen var en han, kaldet en bi-konge, og der var ikke en egentlig forståelse af, hvordan bier reproducerer sig. Det var ikke før det attende århundrede, at europæiske naturfilosoffer begyndte at foretage videnskabelige studier af bifamilier, og herigennem fik en forståelse af biernes komplekse og skjulte biologiske verden. Mens en erhvervsbiavler har flere hundrede bistader, så har et stigende antal parcelhus- og kolonihaveejere et eller to bistader i haven. Placeres staderne med omhu, så generer bierne ikke naboer eller folk, der færdes i haven. Efter invasionen af varroamider i firserne har det ikke været muligt for honningbier at overleve vildt i store dele af Europa. Biernes overlevelse er afhængig af biavlerens aktive bekæmpelse af miderne.
section_prompt_translated: Beekeeping is the maintenance of honeybee families, normally in beehives, by humans. A beekeeper keeps bees with the purpose of collecting honey and beeswax to pollinate crops or to produce bees and bee families in order to sell them to other beekeepers. The place where bees are kept is called the bee farm. The patron saint of beekeeping and beekeepers is Saint Ambrosius. The domestication of bees is depicted in Egyptian art from more than four thousand years ago. For several thousands of years human’s understanding of the biology and ecology of bees was rather limited and this understanding was influenced by superstition and folklore. In ancient times, people believed that the queen bee was a male, called a king bee, and there was no real understanding of how bees reproduced. It was not until the eighteenth century that European natural philosophers began to make scientific studies of bee families and through this gained an understanding of the complex and hidden biological world of bees. While a professional beekeeper has several hundred beehives, an increasing number of house and allotment owners have one or two beehives in their gardens. If the hives are placed with care, then the bees will not disturb neighbours or people who go to the garden. After the invasion of varroa mites in the eighties, it has not been possible for honeybees to survive in the wild over large parts of Europe. The survival of the bees is dependent upon the beekeeper’s active pest control of the mites.

Lokaliteten, hvor bier holdes, kaldes for en bigård. Biavlens og biavleres skytshelgen er Skt. Ambrosius. Domesticering af bier er afbildet i egyptisk kunst for over fire tusind år siden. I adskillige årtusinder var menneskets forståelse af biernes biologi og økologi meget begrænset, og denne forståelse var præget af overtro og folklore. Oldtidens mennesker troede, at bidronningen var en han, kaldet en bi-konge, og der var ikke en egentlig forståelse af, hvordan bier reproducerer sig. Det var ikke før det attende århundrede, at europæiske naturfilosoffer begyndte at foretage videnskabelige studier af bifamilier, og herigennem fik en forståelse af biernes komplekse og skjulte biologiske verden. Mens en erhvervsbiavler har flere hundrede bistader, så har et stigende antal parcelhus- og kolonihaveejere et eller to bistader i haven. Placeres staderne med omhu, så generer bierne ikke naboer eller folk, der færdes i haven. Efter invasionen af varroamider i firserne har det ikke været muligt for honningbier at overleve vildt i store dele af Europa. Biernes overlevelse er afhængig af biavlerens aktive bekæmpelse af miderne.
section_prompt_translated: Beekeeping is the maintenance of honeybee families, normally in beehives, by humans. A beekeeper keeps bees with the purpose of collecting honey and beeswax to pollinate crops or to produce bees and bee families in order to sell them to other beekeepers. The place where bees are kept is called the bee farm. The patron saint of beekeeping and beekeepers is Saint Ambrosius. The domestication of bees is depicted in Egyptian art from more than four thousand years ago. For several thousands of years human’s understanding of the biology and ecology of bees was rather limited and this understanding was influenced by superstition and folklore. In ancient times, people believed that the queen bee was a male, called a king bee, and there was no real understanding of how bees reproduced. It was not until the eighteenth century that European natural philosophers began to make scientific studies of bee families and through this gained an understanding of the complex and hidden biological world of bees. While a professional beekeeper has several hundred beehives, an increasing number of house and allotment owners have one or two beehives in their gardens. If the hives are placed with care, then the bees will not disturb neighbours or people who go to the garden. After the invasion of varroa mites in the eighties, it has not been possible for honeybees to survive in the wild over large parts of Europe. The survival of the bees is dependent upon the beekeeper’s active pest control of the mites.

section_prompt: Een nationale vlag is een vlag die een land vertegenwoordigt. De vlag wordt gevlogen door de overheid, maar kan meestal ook uitgehangen worden door de burgers van dat land. In het verleden ontstonden vlaggen om op het slagveld vriend van vijand te onderscheiden. Het voeren van vlaggen om het land van oorsprong te onderscheiden, buiten gevechtshandelingen om, ontstond toen de marinevlag werd ingevoerd tijdens het zeilvaarttijdperk, in de vroege 17e eeuw. De meeste landen van Europa namen een nationale vlag aan in de loop van de 19e en vroege 20e eeuw, vaak gebaseerd op oudere Middeleeuwse oorlogsvlaggen. De nationale vlag wordt vaak beschreven in de grondwet van een land. Alle nationale vlaggen zijn rechthoekig, behalve de vlag van Nepal. De verhoudingen van de hoogte en de breedte van nationale vlaggen verschillen, maar geen enkele is langer dan zij breed is. De vlaggen van Zwitserland en Vaticaanstad zijn de enige twee nationale vlaggen die precies een vierkant vormen. Vanaf 2011 bestaan alle nationale vlaggen uit op z'n minst twee verschillende kleuren; driekleuren zijn het meest voorkomend. In veel gevallen zijn de kleuren gerangschikt in horizontale of verticale banen.

Deze is gevuld met grond uit vele landen en symboliseert het verlangen om tot eenheid van de mensheid te komen. Jaarlijks wordt op wereldmilieudag aarde uit een nieuw land bijgestort. Op wereldmilieudag in 1977 is op initiatief van de Keniaanse organisatoren een boomplantactie opgezet die woestijnvorming moet tegengaan.

section_prompt: Apelsinimahl on vedelik, mis on saadud apelsinipuu viljast. Sellest tulenevalt soovitatakse piirata apelsinimahla tarbimist ja võimalusel asendada see hoopis puuvilja söömisega. Suurim apelsinimahla tootja ja eksportija maailmas on Brasiilia, ning Euroopa on riigi kõige olulisem eksporditurg.

section_prompt: Kansallislippu on lippu, joka edustaa valtiota tai maata ja toimii sen kansallissymbolina. Kansa omaksui lippujen käytön Ranskan vallankumouksen myötä 1700-luvulla. Tällöin syntyivät kansallisliput ja lippujen kuviointi yksinkertaistui. Kolme neljäsosaa nykyisistä kansallislipuista on toisen maailmansodan jälkeiseltä ajalta ja vain 12 valtiolla on lippu, joka on otettu käyttöön ennen vuotta 1800. Liput ovat lähes aina suorakaiteen muotoisia, toisin kun niitä edeltäneet keskiajan armeijoiden liput, jotka olivat muodoltaan vaihtelevampia. Tänä päivänä ainoana poikkeuksena suorakulman muotoisiin lippuihin on kahdesta kolmiosta muodostuva Nepalin lippu. Sveitsin sekä Vatikaanin liput ovat ainoita neliön muotoisia lippuja. Väreistä suosituimpia ovat valkoinen, sininen, punainen ja vihreä. section_prompt_translated: A national flag is a flag that represents a state or a country and serves as its national symbol. Flags were originally used as signs on the battlefield, and it was not until the 17th century that they began to be used outside of war situations. The people adopted the use of flags with the French Revolution in the 18th century. At that time, the national flags came about, and the design of the flags became more simplified. Three-quarters of current national flags date from time after the Second World War and only 12 states have a flag that was introduced before the year 1800. Denmark has the oldest national flag, which is from the 13th century. National flags can still alter or change in the vicissitudes of history. The constitution most often describes the appearance of the national flag. The flags are almost always rectangular, in contrast to the preceding flags of medieval armies, which were more varied in shape. Today, the only exception to rectangular flags is the flag of Nepal, which consists of two triangles. The flags of Switzerland and the Vatican are the only square flags. The most popular of colors are white, blue, red and green. The flags of some countries have very similar colors and symbols, although the flags are meant to be unique national symbols.

section_prompt_translated: Beekeeping means the raising and care of bees for collecting honey and beeswax. Some also utilize bees to pollinate the crop and as raise them to sell to other beekeepers. Cave paintings depicting the utilization of bees have been found dating back thousands of years. In Egypt, beekeeping was known early on and sealed honey pots have been found in the graves of several pharaohs, such as Tutankhamun. Initially, honey was collected from wild bee nests, but later they learned to build artificial beehives from e.g. hollow tree trunks, straw, and clay pots. Today, frameless hives are built for bees, where honeycombs hang loosely on supports. Beehives consist of sections that are superimposed as a tower. In beekeeping, protective equipment is used to protect from bee stings. However, many beekeepers seem to be desensitized when caring for bees, i.e., the symptoms are eased when stings become constant. According to studies, beekeepers have high levels of antibodies that respond to the main antigen in bee venom. Still, of course, especially those who have had severe reactions need to protect themselves from stings as well as possible.
item_text_translated: Was beekeeping practised in ancient Egypt?

The national flag is often used to demonstrate ownership of a territory. The national flag emerged from the flags of the ships, which were once used to indicate their nationality. National flags can be used for civil, government, and military purposes. Many states therefore use different flags or modifications of the basic form of the national flag for these different areas. In some cases, a distinction is also made between use on land and at sea. The symbolism of the national flag is also often a cause for controversy, for example when the national flag is changed when the form of government changed. section_prompt: Der Imker beschäftigt sich mit der Haltung, Vermehrung und Züchtung von Honigbienen sowie mit der Produktion von Honig und weiterer Bienenprodukte. Wirtschaftlich relevanter ist heute die Bestäubungsleistung der Honigbienen in der Landwirtschaft als Nebenprodukt der Imkerei. Ein Imker braucht keine spezielle Ausbildung, aber in den deutschsprachigen Ländern absolvieren die meisten Neu-Imker einen Grundkurs. Vom Imker zu unterscheiden ist der Zeidler, der den Honig wildlebender Honigbienen-Völker im Wald sammelt. Der Imker hält seine Bienenvölker in künstlichen Nisthöhlen, den Bienenstöcken, in denen Brutnest und Honigvorräte vor Witterungseinflüssen und den Räubereien anderer Tiere geschützt sind. Der Imker produziert mit dem Honig ein Lebensmittel und ist damit in den deutschsprachigen Ländern der strengen Lebensmittelgesetzgebung unterstellt. Honigbienen sind die wichtigsten Bestäuber von Blütenpflanzen. Wegen ihrer Bestäubungsleistung ist die Honigbiene nach Rind und Schwein weltweit das drittwichtigste Nutztier in der Landwirtschaft. Neben der ökologischen Bedeutung der Honigbienen als Bestäuber von Wild- und Kulturpflanzen hat die Imkerei einen großen ökonomischen Nutzen für die Landwirtschaft, wo sie den Ertrag und die Qualität von Obst und Gemüse erhöht.

section_prompt_translated: The beekeeper deals with the keeping, reproduction and breeding of honey bees as well as with the production of honey and other bee products. A beekeeper does not need any special training, but in German-speaking countries most new beekeepers complete a basic course. The beekeeper must be distinguished from the "honey hunter", who collects honey from wild honey bee colonies in the forest. Because of their pollination capacity, the honey bee is the third most important livestock in agriculture worldwide after cattle and pigs. section_prompt: Das Wort Shaka, begleitet von einer typischen Handhaltung, bei der die geschlossene Faust mit abgespreiztem Daumen und kleinem Finger gehoben wird ist eine ganz allgemein auf Hawaii gebräuchliche Geste und etwa so viel bedeutet wie „Cool!“ oder „Locker!“. Unter Windsurfern ist das Zeichen als Gruß verbreitet und wird als „Hang Loose“ bezeichnet. Hier hat dieser Gruß jedoch eine ganz reale Anwendung: die abgespreizten Finger stehen für den Trapez-Tampen und die Faust für den Haken des Trapezes, mit welchem sich der Windsurfer einhängt. Der exakte Ursprung ist letztlich nicht gesichert, doch existieren eine Reihe von Theorien. Nach Recherche einer Zeitung geht das Handzeichen auf einen berühmten Hawaiier zurück, dem an einer Hand drei Finger fehlten. Woher aber der begleitende Name Shaka rührt, ist ungeklärt. Auch von Prominenten wurde der Gruß häufig verwendet. Bekannte Schauspieler, Musiker und Politiker verwendeten ihn und selbst der brasilianische Weltfußballer Ronaldinho nutzte diese Geste of beim Torjubel. Er schwenkte jedoch seine beiden Hände noch zusätzlich.
section_prompt_translated: The word Shaka, accompanied by a typical hand position in which the closed fist is raised with the thumb and little finger spread, is a gesture commonly used in Hawaii and means something like "cool" or "relaxed". The sign is common among windsurfers as a greeting and is referred to as "Hang Loose". Here, however, this greeting has a very real application: the splayed fingers stand for the trapeze rope and the fist for the hook of the trapeze with which the windsurfer attaches himself. The exact origin of the sign is ultimately not certain, but a number of theories exist. According to a newspaper research, the hand sign goes back to a famous Hawaiian who was missing three fingers on one hand. But where the accompanying name Shaka comes from is unclear. The greeting is also often used by celebrities. Well-known actors, musicians and politicians use it and even the Brazilian world footballer Ronaldinho often used this gesture when celebrating goals. However, he waved both of his hands in addition.

section_prompt: Das Monokelist eine Sehhilfe, die im Gegensatz zur heute verwendeten Brille aus nur einem Glas besteht und am Auge eingeklemmt wird. Das Monokel entwickelte sich aus dem Lesestein, einer geschliffenen Linse aus Quarz oder Beryll, daher das deutsche Wort Brille. Dieser wurde zum Vergrößern direkt auf das Schriftstück gelegt. Das im Deutschen verwendete Wort Monokel wurde aus dem Fränzösischem entlehnt, entstand aber ursprünglich als zweisprachiges Kunstwort aus dem Altgrichischen und Latein. Das Monokel war gegen Ende des 19. Jahrhunderts besonders in Deutschland und Großbritannien populär und galt als ein Statussymbol der höheren Gesellschaftsschichten. Besonders verbreitet war es in den Offizierkorps der Armeen dieser beiden Länder. Einige Mediziner waren damals der Meinung, das Verzerren des Gesichts zum Festhalten des Monokels sei gesundheitsschädlich. Dagegen wurde gewöhnlich argumentiert, dass nur Personen Monokel tragen sollten, die es ohne solche Gesichtsverzerrungen tragen könnten. Dem wurde von Seiten der Optiker auch durch unterschiedliche Größen entsprochen.
section_prompt_translated: The monocle is a visual aid that, in contrast to the glasses used today, consists of only one lens and is clamped on the eye. The monocle developed from the reading stone, a cut lens made of quartz or beryl. This is where the German word "Brille" comes from. This reading stone was placed directly on the document to enlarge it. The word monocle used in German was borrowed from French, but originally came about as a bilingual made-up word from ancient Greek and Latin. The monocle was particularly popular in Germany and Great Britain towards the end of the 19th century and was considered a status symbol for the upper classes of society. It was particularly widespread in the officer corps of the armies of these two countries. At the time, some medical professionals were of the opinion that contorting the face to hold the monocle was harmful to health. Conversely, it was commonly argued that monocles should only be worn by people who could wear them without such facial distortions. The opticians also resolved this with different sizes.

instrument: MECO L1 (Multilingual Eye-movement Corpus, first-language reading task): yes/no comprehension questions
section_prompt: Der Imker beschäftigt sich mit der Haltung, Vermehrung und Züchtung von Honigbienen sowie mit der Produktion von Honig und weiterer Bienenprodukte. Wirtschaftlich relevanter ist heute die Bestäubungsleistung der Honigbienen in der Landwirtschaft als Nebenprodukt der Imkerei. Ein Imker braucht keine spezielle Ausbildung, in den deutschsprachigen Ländern absolvieren aber die meisten Neu-Imker einen Grundkurs. Vom Imker zu unterscheiden ist der Zeidler, der den Honig wild lebender Honigbienen-Völker im Wald sammelt. Der Imker hält seine Bienenvölker in künstlichen Nisthöhlen, den Bienenstöcken, in denen Brutnest und Honigvorräte vor Witterungseinflüssen und den Räubereien anderer Tiere geschützt sind. Der Imker produziert mit dem Honig ein Lebensmittel und ist damit in den deutschsprachigen Ländern der strengen Lebensmittelgesetzgebung unterstellt. Honigbienen sind die wichtigsten Bestäuber von den Blütenpflanzen. Wegen ihrer Bestäubungsleistung ist die Honigbiene nach Rind und Schwein weltweit das drittwichtigste Nutztier in der Landwirtschaft. Neben der ökologischen Bedeutung der Honigbienen als Bestäuber von Wild- und Kulturpflanzen hat die Imkerei einen großen ökonomischen Nutzen für die Landwirtschaft, wo sie den Ertrag und die Qualität von Obst und Gemüse erhöht.
section_prompt_translated: The beekeeper deals with the keeping, reproduction and breeding of honey bees as well as with the production of honey and other bee products. More economically relevant today is the pollination performance of honey bees in agriculture as a by-product of beekeeping. A beekeeper does not need any special training, but in German-speaking countries most new beekeepers complete a basic course. The beekeeper must be distinguished from the "honey hunter", who collects honey from wild honey bee colonies in the forest. The beekeeper keeps his bee colonies in artificial nesting holes, the beehives, in which brood nests and honey stores are protected from the weather and the robberies of other animals. The beekeeper uses the honey to produce food and is therefore subject to strict food legislation in German-speaking countries. Honey bees are the main pollinators of flowering plants. Because of their pollination capacity, the honey bee is the third most important livestock in agriculture worldwide after cattle and pigs. In addition to the ecological importance of honey bees as pollinators of wild and cultivated plants, beekeeping has great economic benefits for agriculture, where it increases the yield and quality of fruit and vegetables.

Η προέλευση των σημαιών ιστορικά σχετίζεται με το πεδίο της μάχης στο οποίο οι σημαίες αποτελούσαν τα στρατιωτικά σύμβολα των αντιμαχόμενων πλευρών. Η ανάρτηση των σημαιών εκτός πεδίου μάχης καθιερώθηκε μόλις στις αρχές του δέκατου έβδομου αιώνα. Η σημαία της κάθε χώρας συνήθως περιγράφεται στο σύνταγμα της χώρας της. Το σχήμα όλων των σημαιών είναι ορθογώνιο, με μοναδική εξαίρεση τη σημαία του Νεπάλ που έχει τριγωνικό σχήμα. Οι διαστάσεις των σημαιών δεν είναι προκαθορισμένες, με αποτέλεσμα να παρουσιάζεται ποικιλία στο μήκος και το πλάτος τους. Στις σημαίες μάλιστα δύο χωρών, της Ελβετίας και του Βατικανού, το μήκος είναι ίσο με το πλάτος. Το κόκκινο, το άσπρο, το πράσινο και το μπλε αποτελούν τα συνήθη χρώματα των σημαιών. Παρόλο που η εθνική σημαία αποτελεί ένα μοναδικό σύμβολο για τη χώρα που αντιπροσωπεύει, εντούτοις παρατηρούνται σημαίες με παρόμοια χρώματα και σχέδια.

Τη δεκαετία του 1960, οι σέρφερ που επισκέπτονταν τη Χαβάη, «δανείστηκαν» το τοπικό αυτό νεύμα, το οποίο διαδόθηκε σε όλο τον κόσμο. Έκτοτε, το νεύμα αυτό χρησιμοποιείται ευρέως μεταξύ των ανθρώπων για ανταλλαγή χαιρετισμών, έκφραση ευχαριστιών ή δήλωση επαίνου. Οι πολίτες της Χαβάη χρησιμοποιούν το νεύμα σάκα για να εκφράσουν συγχρόνως αυτό που αποκαλούν «Aloha Spirit», δηλαδή τη φιλία, την κατανόηση, τη συμπόνια και την αλληλεγγύη μεταξύ των διαφόρων φυλών που ζουν στη Χαβάη. section_prompt_translated: The Hawaiian shaka sign is used by surf lovers, usually during a friendly conversation, to portray that “everything is under control”. To do the shaka sign, you should raise the first and last finger of your hand, keep the middle fingers bent and rotate your hand left and right. During the 1960s, surfers who visited Hawaii “borrowed” this local shake, which was then distributed worldwide. Since then, this sign is vastly used between people for greetings, expressions of gratitude, or praise declarations. Hawaiians use the shaka sign to express simultaneously what they call the “Aloha Spirit” for friendship, understanding, compassion and solidarity between different nations that live in Hawaii. It is believed that the shaka sign originated from Spanish immigrants, who, to invite native Hawaiians for a drink, used to bring their raised thumb close to their lips, keeping their middle fingers closed.
item_text_translated: Did the Spanish immigrants “borrow” the shaka gesture from the Hawaiians?

section_prompt_translated: The largest carnivorous animal of modern times has a pouch and is called thylacine. It is commonly known as the Tasmanian tiger or wolf due to its resemblance to the tiger (striped back) or the wolf (characteristics). Fossils show that the thylacine lived in mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Guinea until the twentieth century and has since been considered an endangered species. As well as females, male thylacines had a pouch. For example, the pouch was used to protect its external reproductive organs during hunting for the male thylacine. The thylacine is characterized by increased survival capacities, as it secures its food even in extremely sparsely populated areas. The significant reduction or extinction of the thylacine from Australia is estimated before British colonialism, whereas in Tasmania, it continued to survive. Cash rewards for thylacine hunting, the spread of diseases, the appearance of dogs and human intervention in the environment are considered to be some of the causes of thylacine extinction. Although it is officially considered an extinct species, there is evidence to the contrary - but information remains unconfirmed.

The use of monocles was associated with the aristocracy of the nineteenth-century. The aristocrats of that time used to wear a hat, a long coat and the characteristic monocle that completed their appearance/look. Also, army officers during that period, used to circulate with one monocle on the eye. Nowadays, the monocle is not commonly used. The significant progress that has been marked in the optometric field, currently allows the accurate recording of visual function and consequently, the creation of glasses and contact lenses with different characteristics for each eye.

section_prompt: Η μελισσοκομία αφορά τη συγκέντρωση μελισσών σε κυψέλες, ιδίως εκείνων που παράγουν μέλι. Ο μελισσοκόμος συγκεντρώνει τις μέλισσες για διάφορους λόγους όπως η συλλογή μελιού και των παραγόμενων από την κυψέλη προϊόντων (π.χ., κηρήθρα), η επικονίαση καλλιεργειών και η πώληση των μελισσών σε άλλους μελισσοκόμους. Η μελισσοκομία έχει αρκετά παλιά παράδοση, αφού απεικονίζεται σε ζωγραφικές παραστάσεις τεσσάρων χιλιάδων ετών που ανακαλύφθηκαν στην Αίγυπτο. Στα παλιά χρόνια, η συλλογή του μελιού γινόταν από φυσικές κυψέλες με τη βοήθεια του καπνού και το μέλι αποθηκευόταν σε δοχεία, μερικά από τα οποία βρέθηκαν στις πυραμίδες του Φαραώ. Μετά τον δέκατο όγδοο αιώνα, η μελέτη της βιολογίας των μελισσών οδήγησε στην εφεύρεση τεχνητών κυψελών στην Ευρώπη, οι οποίες επέτρεπαν τη συγκομιδή του μελιού χωρίς την καταστροφή ολόκληρης της αποικίας μελισσών. Στις μέρες μας, ορισμένοι μελισσοκόμοι υποστηρίζουν ότι αποκτούν ανοσία στα τσιμπήματα και ότι είναι σημαντικό για την ασφάλειά τους να δέχονται κάθε χρόνο ορισμένα τσιμπήματα από μέλισσες. Τα ευρήματα πρόσφατων ερευνών υποστηρίζουν ότι οι μελισσοκόμοι έχουν υψηλά επίπεδα αντισωμάτων, τα οποία μάλιστα αποτελούν και το αντίδοτο στο κεντρί της μέλισσας.

section_prompt_translated: In the Roman mythology and religion, Janus is the god of beginnings and of gates. Janus was responsible for the beginnings and endings of conflict, and therefore also of war and peace. The doors of his temple were open during war and closed in times of peace. As the god of gates, he was also associated with entering and exiting the doors of the home. Janus often symbolised changes and transitions, such as the move from one rank to another, one vision to another, and growing from youth into adulthood. The Romans worshipped Janus at the beginning of the harvest and during planting, as well as at weddings, deaths, and other beginnings. There was no priest devoted solely to Janus, but the high priest himself carried out his rituals. Janus symbolised the midpoint between barbarity and civilisation, rural and urban areas, youth and maturity. The Ancient Greeks did not have an equivalent god to Janus, and the Romans claimed he was unique to them.

section_prompt_translated: In the Roman mythology and religion, Janus is the god of beginnings and of gates. He has a dual nature and is generally depicted as having two faces, because he looks to the future and the past. Janus was responsible for the beginnings and endings of conflict, and therefore also of war and peace. The doors of his temple were open during war and closed in times of peace. As the god of gates, he was also associated with entering and exiting the doors of the home. Janus often symbolised changes and transitions, such as the move from one rank to another, one vision to another, and growing from youth into adulthood. The Romans worshipped Janus at the beginning of the harvest and during planting, as well as at weddings, deaths, and other beginnings. There was no priest devoted solely to Janus, but the high priest himself carried out his rituals. Janus symbolised the midpoint between barbarity and civilisation, rural and urban areas, youth and maturity. The Ancient Greeks did not have an equivalent god to Janus, and the Romans claimed he was unique to them.

section_prompt_translated: A national flag is the official flag of a country. The flag of a country is usually flown on public institutions, such as schools and courthouses. The flag is typically composed of symbols and shapes that symbolise the history of the country or the ideology that they hold. Although most citizens see the flag as a way to distinguish their country, often different national flags are very similar to each other. For example, the flags of Monaco, Indonesia and Poland have very similar designs, as do the flags of Ireland and the Ivory Coast. Most national flags have three colours. The most common colours are blue, white and red. Generally, most citizens of a country have great respect for their national flag. For example, in most of the world's countries it is traditional that if the national flag is flown with other flags, it will be raised first and lowered last. In addition, when it is flown with the flags of other countries, it will be flown in the centre. Traditions and symbols often include use of the flag. For example, hanging the flag upside down is usually a sign of distress, and lowering the flag to half mast is a symbol of national mourning. Some countries have passed laws to prevent desecration of the national flag, such as laws against burning the flag or laws stating that the flag must not touch the ground.

The shaka sign is made with the hand, with the thumb and the little finger stretched out in opposite directions, and the three other fingers curled in towards the palm. Sometimes the hand is rotated back and forth around the axis of the wrist, for emphasis. The origin of the sign is uncertain. One explanation claims that the gesture comes from when local residents placed floral neckalces on the shoulders of their guests. In order to place the wreath over the head of the guest with one hand, the three central fingers held the wreath, while the thumb and little finger were spread out to the sides to open up the circle of the wreath. According to another version, a local fisherman who lost three fingers in a work accident, used to wave his hand with only his thumb and little finger, and children who copied his movements created the sign. Other versions claims that Spanish settlers created the sign as an invitation to a drink, while a particularly gruesome version claims that one of the first surfers waved for help with a similar gesture, after a shark bit off his middle fingers. The residents of the state of Hawaii in the United States typically use the shaka sign as a visualisation of the spirit of Aloha, that is as a sign of friendship and solidarity between the various races who live on the islands. Depending on context, the the sign can convey thanks, a greeting, or simply to wave hello.

section_prompt_translated: The shaka sign, also known as "be cool", is a gesture performed with one hand. It is common primarily in the islands of Hawaii in the United States, but it can typically be seen as a wordless greeting, commonly used around the world between surfers and windsurfers and especially between divers. The shaka sign is made with the hand, with the thumb and the little finger stretched out in opposite directions, and the three other fingers curled in towards the palm. Sometimes the hand is rotated back and forth around the axis of the wrist, for emphasis. The origin of the sign is uncertain. One explanation claims that the gesture comes from when local residents placed floral neckalces on the shoulders of their guests. In order to place the wreath over the head of the guest with one hand, the three central fingers held the wreath, while the thumb and little finger were spread out to the sides to open up the circle of the wreath. According to another version, a local fisherman who lost three fingers in a work accident, used to wave his hand with only his thumb and little finger, and children who copied his movements created the sign. Other versions claims that Spanish settlers created the sign as an invitation to a drink, while a particularly gruesome version claims that one of the first surfers waved for help with a similar gesture, after a shark bit off his middle fingers. The residents of the state of Hawaii in the United States typically use the shaka sign as a visualisation of the spirit of Aloha, that is as a sign of friendship and solidarity between the various races who live on the islands. Depending on context, the the sign can convey thanks, a greeting, or simply to wave hello.

section_prompt_translated: The shaka sign, also known as "be cool", is a gesture performed with one hand. It is common primarily in the islands of Hawaii in the United States, but it can typically be seen as a wordless greeting, commonly used around the world between surfers and windsurfers and especially between divers. The shaka sign is made with the hand, with the thumb and the little finger stretched out in opposite directions, and the three other fingers curled in towards the palm. Sometimes the hand is rotated back and forth around the axis of the wrist, for emphasis. The origin of the sign is uncertain. One explanation claims that the gesture comes from when local residents placed floral neckalces on the shoulders of their guests. In order to place the wreath over the head of the guest with one hand, the three central fingers held the wreath, while the thumb and little finger were spread out to the sides to open up the circle of the wreath. According to another version, a local fisherman who lost three fingers in a work accident, used to wave his hand with only his thumb and little finger, and children who copied his movements created the sign. Other versions claims that Spanish settlers created the sign as an invitation to a drink, while a particularly gruesome version claims that one of the first surfers waved for help with a similar gesture, after a shark bit off his middle fingers. The residents of the state of Hawaii in the United States typically use the shaka sign as a visualisation of the spirit of Aloha, that is as a sign of friendship and solidarity between the various races who live on the islands. Depending on context, the the sign can convey thanks, a greeting, or simply to wave hello.

section_prompt_translated: The Tasmanian wolf is a mammal that apparently went extinct during the twentieth century. It is classified as a marsupial and is thought to be the largest predatory marsupial in the modern era. The Tasmanian wolf went extinct in Australia a few thousand years before European settlers came to the continent, but it survived on the island of Tasmania, alongside other species such as the Tasmanian devil. Researchers estimate that it became fully extinct during the the third decade of the last century, primarily due to intensive hunting that was encouraged with cash prizes. Additional causes for the extinction were diseases, the arrival of dogs on the island, and the encroachment of humans on their territories. The Tasmanian wolf was similar in appearance to a large dog with short fur and a stiff tail. It's brownish-yellow coat included about twenty dark stripes, that crossed the back, haunches and the base of the tail. These stripes were clearest on young animals, and they faded with age. Although no recordings of the Tasmanian wolf's voice exist, reports on the wolves' behaviour in its natural environs and in captivity claim that the wolves would roar and whistle when aroused or excited. While hunting, they would utter a series of short vocalisations that sounded like gutteral barks reminiscent of a cough, that apparently served to communicate with the other members of the pack.

section_prompt_translated: The Tasmanian wolf is a mammal that apparently went extinct during the twentieth century. It is classified as a marsupial and is thought to be the largest predatory marsupial in the modern era. The Tasmanian wolf went extinct in Australia a few thousand years before European settlers came to the continent, but it survived on the island of Tasmania, alongside other species such as the Tasmanian devil. Researchers estimate that it became fully extinct during the the third decade of the last century, primarily due to intensive hunting that was encouraged with cash prizes. Additional causes for the extinction were diseases, the arrival of dogs on the island, and the encroachment of humans on their territories. The Tasmanian wolf was similar in appearance to a large dog with short fur and a stiff tail. It's brownish-yellow coat included about twenty dark stripes, that crossed the back, haunches and the base of the tail. These stripes were clearest on young animals, and they faded with age. Although no recordings of the Tasmanian wolf's voice exist, reports on the wolves' behaviour in its natural environs and in captivity claim that the wolves would roar and whistle when aroused or excited. While hunting, they would utter a series of short vocalisations that sounded like gutteral barks reminiscent of a cough, that apparently served to communicate with the other members of the pack.

section_prompt_translated: World environment day is an international event held every year on June fifth. This day is celebrated by the UN member countries, and it serves as a tool to raise awareness about the environment. The day was founded by the UN general assembly in the early seventies. On this day meetings and conferences are held to educate and raise awareness about environmental issues, including ways to cope with and prevent environmental problems. The goal of this day is to raise awareness about issues relating to the environment, to change environmental policy and encourage cooperation between countries, to ensure that people will continue to enjoy a prosperous and safe world. World environment day is noted around the world with various activities, such as outdoor concerts, processions, tree plantings, writing and poster-making competitions in school, and recycling and clean-up campaigns. Every year, a theme is chosen that serves as a guiding theme for all the activities held around the world. For example, in 2018 the motto was: "Beating plastic pollution", and the day was devoted to raising awareness to the damage caused by plastic-based refuse and the importance of recycling. The day was crowned a great success, and many countries followed it by pledging to reduce plastic use significantly over the next five years.

section_prompt_translated: World environment day is an international event held every year on June fifth. This day is celebrated by the UN member countries, and it serves as a tool to raise awareness about the environment. The day was founded by the UN general assembly in the early seventies. On this day meetings and conferences are held to educate and raise awareness about environmental issues, including ways to cope with and prevent environmental problems. The goal of this day is to raise awareness about issues relating to the environment, to change environmental policy and encourage cooperation between countries, to ensure that people will continue to enjoy a prosperous and safe world. World environment day is noted around the world with various activities, such as outdoor concerts, processions, tree plantings, writing and poster-making competitions in school, and recycling and clean-up campaigns. Every year, a theme is chosen that serves as a guiding theme for all the activities held around the world. For example, in 2018 the motto was: "Beating plastic pollution", and the day was devoted to raising awareness to the damage caused by plastic-based refuse and the importance of recycling. The day was crowned a great success, and many countries followed it by pledging to reduce plastic use significantly over the next five years.
item_text_translated: Is Environment Day celebrated on a different day each year?

item_text: האם ענידת מונוקול היתה מלווה בדרך כלל בלבישת טוקסידו?
section_prompt_translated: A monocle is a type of spectacles used to correct vision in one eye only. It is comprised of a round lens and is usually surrounded by a maetal frame that enables the attachment of a string. The other end of the string is attached to the clothing of the wearer to prevent loss of the monocle. The monocle was common at the end of the nineteenth century but is very rarely used today. This is primarily due to advances in optometry that allow for better measurement of visual acuity, and also due to the ability to produce glasses and contact lenses with different strengths for each eye. The monocle is kept in place by the facial muscles of the wearer, with the size of the monocle designed to remain in place between the brow and cheek of the wearer with a slight winking action. Due to this method of use, the monocle can easily fall off due to an inappropriate facial expression. The use of the monocle was primarily associated with rich upper-class men. Towards the end of the nineteenth century, the use of the monocle was paired with a tuxedo and top hat, which completed the stereotypical outfit of an English gentleman.

section_prompt: מיץ תפוזים הוא מיץ פירות המופק מסחיטת תפוזים. הוא נפוץ במדינות רבות בעולם, ובמקומות רבים נהוג לשתות אותו בארוחת הבוקר. ברזיל היא המובילה בייצוא של מיץ תפוזים, ואחריה ארצות הברית. כוס מיץ ממוצעת מכילה כשניים וחצי תפוזים. בניגוד לייצור ביתי של מיץ תפוזים הכולל אך ורק סחיטה של תפוזים טריים, ייצורו המסחרי כולל מספר שלבים מורכבים. בשלב הראשון, לאחר סחיטת התפוזים, המיץ עובר תהליך פיסטור וסינון. לאחר שלב זה, המיץ עובר תהליך אידוי בתנאי ריק וחום. לאחר אידוי רוב המים בתערובת המיץ, נותר תרכיז אשר מרבית משקלו מקורה בסוכר סוכר. תרכיז זה מאוכסן בהקפאה בטמפרטורה של מינוס עשר מעלות. לעיתים, בתום תהליך האידוי מוסיפים לתערובת תמציות, ויטמין C ושמנים כדי להשיב לחומר תכונות של טעם וערך תזונתי. ישנם מחקרים רבים סותרים בנוגע ליתרונותיו הבריאותיים של צריכה יומית של מיץ תפוזים. מצד אחד, המיץ מכיל כמויות מכובדות של ויטמינים. אך מצד שני, מיץ תפוזים מכיל כמויות סוכר גבוהות, אשר דומות למשקאות ממותקים מלאכותיים. לכן, רוב מומחי הבריאות ממליצים לצרוך את הפרי בצורתו הגולמית, ולא בצורת מיץ.
item_text: האם ישנם יתרונות בריאותיים ברורים בשתיית מיץ תפוזים?
section_prompt_translated: Orange juice is a fruit juice produced by squeezing oranges. It is common in many countries around the world, and in many places it is customary to drink it with breakfast. Brazil is the lead exporter of orange juice, followed by the United States. A typical glass of juice contains about two and half oranges. In contrast to homemade production of orange juice that only includes squeezing fresh oranges, the commercial production includes a number of complex stages. In the first stage, after squeezing the oranges, the juice is pasteurised and strained. After this stage, the juice is evaporated under vacuum and heat. After evaporating most of the water from the juice mixture, there remains a concentrate comprised mostly of sugar. This concentrate is stored frozen at minus ten degrees. Often, after evaporation extracts, vitamin C and oils are added to restore the flavour and nutritional value of the substance. There is much contradictory research regarding the health benefits of drinking orange juice on a daily basis. On one hand, the juice contains significant amounts of vitamins. On the other hand, orange juice contains high levels of sugar, similar to artificially sweetened drinks. Therefore most health experts recommend consuming the fruit in its raw form, and not as juice.
item_text_translated: Are there clear health benefits to drinking orange juice?

section_prompt: דבוראות היא ענף בחקלאות העוסק בגידול דבורים מבויתות. מטרת הדבוראות היא הפקת תוצרים מכוורת הדבורים. רוב העוסקים בענף מגדלים דבורים לצורך הפקת דבש, אשר לו מגוון שימושים נרחב, כמקור לתזונה, כמרכיב במשקאות ובמתכונים וגם ברפואה. מוצר נפוץ נוסף הוא שעוות הדבורים, שמשמשת לייצור נרות כמו גם לייצור מוצרים בתחום הטקסטיל. מקצוע הדבוראות דורש מאמץ פיזי: לפי הערכות כוורת אחת אינה דורשת יותר משני ימי עבודה בשנה, אולם דבוראי מטפל לרוב במספר רב של כוורות, המפוזרות על פני מרחק רב. בנוסף, העבודה מאופיינת בהעתקת מיקום הכוורות מאזור מרעה אחד לאחר, בניית קומות של כוורות, ורדיית דבש, כאשר אחד הקשיים הגדולים הוא ביצוע העבודות בעת לבישת סרבל מגן המגביל את התנועה ומקשה על ביצוע העבודה. למרות המגבלה על התנועה, לבישת הסרבל קריטית על מנת להגן על העוסקים בדבוראות מעקיצות דבורים. בנוסף לסרבל, דבוראים לובשים מסכת רשת על מנת להגן על פניהם ובפרט על אזור העיניים. עם זאת, לעיתים רחוקות בלבד ילבשו דבוראים כפפות מגן. הסיבה לכך היא שעבודה בידיים חשופות מאפשרת חופש פעולה בעת פתיחת הכוורת במטרה לבחון את מצב המושבה ולהתבונן בתנועת משפחת הדבורים.
item_text: האם דבוראות רווחית רק לצורכי ייצור דברי מאכל?
section_prompt_translated: Beekeeping is a branch in agriculture that deals with farming domesticated bees. The goal of beekeeping is the production of commodities from the beehive. Most of the practitioners in the field raise bees for the production of honey, which has a wide variety of uses, as a source of nutrition, as an ingredient in drinks and recipes and also in medicine. Another common product is beeswax, that is used in the production of candles as well as the products in the textile industry. The beekeeping profession is physically demanding: according to estimates a single hive does not need more than two days of labour per year, but a beekeeper usually takes care of a large number of hives, spread over a large distance. Additionally, the work necessitates moving the hives from one pasture to another, building of the hives, and harvesting the honey, with one of the greatest challenges being carrying out the labour while wearing protective clothing that limits movement and makes the labour more difficult. Despite the limitations on movement, wearing the suit is critical to protect the beekeepers from bee stings. In addition to the suit, beekeepers wear a net mask to protect their face and especially their eyes. Beekeepers rarely wear gloves, however. The reason for this is that working with bare hands allows the dexterity to open the hive in order to check on the status of the colony and examine the movement of the bee family.
item_text_translated: Is beekeeping profitable only for producing foodstuffs?

item_text: האם דבוראי מטפל בדרך כלל במספר רב של כוורות?
section_prompt_translated: Beekeeping is a branch in agriculture that deals with farming domesticated bees. The goal of beekeeping is the production of commodities from the beehive. Most of the practitioners in the field raise bees for the production of honey, which has a wide variety of uses, as a source of nutrition, as an ingredient in drinks and recipes and also in medicine. Another common product is beeswax, that is used in the production of candles as well as the products in the textile industry. The beekeeping profession is physically demanding: according to estimates a single hive does not need more than two days of labour per year, but a beekeeper usually takes care of a large number of hives, spread over a large distance. Additionally, the work necessitates moving the hives from one pasture to another, building of the hives, and harvesting the honey, with one of the greatest challenges being carrying out the labour while wearing protective clothing that limits movement and makes the labour more difficult. Despite the limitations on movement, wearing the suit is critical to protect the beekeepers from bee stings. In addition to the suit, beekeepers wear a net mask to protect their face and especially their eyes. Beekeepers rarely wear gloves, however. The reason for this is that working with bare hands allows the dexterity to open the hive in order to check on the status of the colony and examine the movement of the bee family.

section_prompt_translated: Tasmanian wolves were large marsupials native to Papua New Guinea, the Australian mainland, and Tasmania. Tasmanian wolves disappeared from the Australian continent about two thousand years ago, believed to have been outmatched by the dingo dog. The Tasmanian wolves’ survival may have been adversely affected not only by dingo dogs but also the growing population, improved hunting and working methods and the settlement of Europeans in Tasmania at the turn of the twentieth century. Europeans bred sheep which the Tasmanian wolf preyed on, making them disliked. But later it was thought that dogs that the Europeans brought with them became predators as well and may have attacked the lambs. Tasmanian wolves preferred hunting birds, but it is possible that lambs became their prey also. As consequence of the bad reputation, hunters received rewards for every Tasmanian wolf they caught. As well as hunting to prevent livestock attacks, other factors, such as competition with European wild dogs and habitat loss, contributed to the species decline and extinction. Both the last captive and wild Tasmanian wolves died in the early twentieth century and since there was more no solid evidence to support Tasmanian wolves’ existence, the species was declared extinct.

section_prompt: 국기는 한 국가를 상징하는 깃발을 말한다. 과거에는 삼각형의 깃발을 많이 썼지만, 최근에는 네팔의 경우를 제외하고는 대부분 직사각형 모양의 깃발을 사용하고 있다. 가로세로 비율은 나라마다 조금씩 다르나 세로가 가로보다 큰 국기는 없다. 한편 스위스와 바티칸만 정사각형의 국기를 사용한다. 가로세로의 비율을 무시하고 대개 3:2로 그려 놓는 것처럼 나라별 국기의 미세한 차이도 무시하고 빨강이면 다 같은 빨강, 파랑이면 다 같은 파랑으로 표시하는 경우가 많은데, 엄연히 이는 잘못이다. 예를 들어 같은 빨강이라도 미국의 국기에 들어있는 빨강과, 영국 유니언잭에 있는 빨강, 프랑스 삼색기의 빨강이 모두 다르다. 미국의 빨강은 노란 빛이 줄고 파란 빛이 좀더 많이 섞이고 검정도 아주 살짝 첨가된, 약간 자색 같은 빨강이지만 영국은 좀더 순수 빨강에 가까운 색이며, 프랑스는 노랑이 많이 섞인 밝은 분위기의 빨강이다. 이렇게 나라마다 많이 쓰는 색깔이 있고 그 땅에서 산출되는 염료의 종류도 다르고 좋아하는 색깔도 달라서 미세한 색상의 차이가 있었고 과거에는 이를 세세하게 따지지 않았으나, 색상학과 인쇄술이 발달한 요즘은 나라마다 국기에 쓰인 색의 지정색을 법으로 정해 놓은 경우가 많다. 다만 무채색의 양끝인 검정과 하양은 순수 검정과 순수 하양을 쓰는 것이 대부분이다.
